text:
sam: Deploybot alerted p95+ latency in canary for v3.6.2 — spike started ~5m ago. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/ABCD. Thinking we need an abort + rollback. Thoughts?
deploy-bot: Auto-check triggered: canary p95 = 720ms (baseline 210ms). Error rate +1.8%. Recommend: AUTO-ROLLBACK if operator not present in 2m. Reason: kernel flag change -> kvcache regrowth.
kai: oncall here, joining. Can we confirm it's not a metric anomaly? Any correlating traces?
maria: I'm seeing increased tail on model-serving worker logs same timeframe. stack traces show OOM-ish GC pauses on a subset of hosts.
sam: ok, that aligns with kvcache churn hypothesis. We should NOT roll forward. Prefer pin to v3.6.1 and rollback canary -> full if symptoms persist.
ashley: I can run the rollback. Two questions: 1) do we want automated rollback to fire now or hold for manual confirmation? 2) who is authorizing customer-facing comms?
sam: hold for manual. deploy-bot has auto window but we override. I'm authorizing. Ash, can you do the rollback and post the commands you run? Also update release notes draft for the rollback.
deploy-bot: Note: Auto-rollback timer paused by user override at T+120s. Manual operator action required.
kai: For safety, do a staged rollback: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 3min observation. Use traffic-slice --route canary flag.
maria: Agree. Also verify model weights checksum on v3.6.1 before traffic shift. I can run checks while Ash does cut.
ashley: Copy. Workflow I'll follow: 1) pin service tag to v3.6.1 2) shift canary traffic to pinned route 3) scale down v3.6.2 replicas 4) observe metrics 5) open rollback PR notes. Command snippets below:
```
# pin service
redwoodctl service pin --service inference-api --version v3.6.1 --reason "canary p95 regression"
# shift traffic slice
redwoodctl traffic shift --service inference-api --from v3.6.2 --to v3.6.1 --percent 10 --wait 180s
```
kai: keep the deploybot hook open so it can re-evaluate and stop if things worsen.
maria: checksums OK for v3.6.1 on eu-west-1 and us-west-2. No mismatches.
sam: Customer comms: I'll draft a short blurb mentioning limited canary rollback, no data exposure, ETA for full rollback if needed. Ash, pls add to release-notes/rollback-notes.md and ping support.
deploy-bot: Observability: starting telemetry replay for the affected window. Attaching summary when ready.
ashley: Executing now. Pasted logs:
```
[2025-11-12T13:14:22Z] Action: pin service inference-api -> v3.6.1 (operator ashley)
[2025-11-12T13:14:25Z] Traffic shift start: 10% -> v3.6.1
[2025-11-12T13:17:30Z] Observed p95 drop from 720ms -> 240ms in canary slice
[2025-11-12T13:17:31Z] Traffic shift to 50% initiated
```
kai: nice, keep 3min windows between steps. If error rate increases >0.5% absolute, abort and roll to safe fallback (v3.6.0) and open incident.
maria: logs show fewer GC stalls on v3.6.1. Looks stable so far.
sam: Good. I notified support and legal that we're doing a canary rollback. Draft message pinned in #support: "We rolled canary to v3.6.1 due to latency regression observed. Monitoring.": @support please escalate if you see user reports.
ashley: Completed 100% canary rollback at 13:24Z. Final metrics: p95 230ms, errors within baseline. I created rollback-notes PR: https://git.redwood/rollbacks/PR-412.
deploy-bot: Auto-rollback disabled for this release until postmortem complete (operator: sam). Recommendation: run localized regression evals on v3.6.2 before reattempt.
sam: Next steps: 1) block v3.6.2 in release calendar, 2) create a postmortem ticket with perf traces and kernel-flag diffs, 3) coordinate a patch release (3.6.3) if root cause identified, 4) update release notes to reflect rollback and user impact (none). I'll assign owners.
kai: I'll schedule the postmortem meeting and add oncall rotation.
maria: I'll start the root-cause delta between v3.6.1 and v3.6.2 (kernel flags + quantization kernel changes).
ashley: Closing thread. If deploy-bot re-suggests rollback, re-open and ping me.
oncall-bot: Reminder: open incident ticket required for manual rollback events. Created INC-2025-084.
sam: Thanks team :thumbsup:
